name: Spaghetti Bolognese
blurb: Slow-simmered beef and pork ragu with a glossy tomato sauce over spaghetti.
ingredients: Parmesan and olive oil, to serve
method: Heat 2 tbsp olive oil in a large pan and gently fry the onion, carrot and celery for 8-10 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic for 1 minute, then turn up the heat and add both minces, breaking them up and browning well.
Stir in the tomato puree and cook for 2 minutes, then pour in the wine and let it bubble away.
Add the chopped tomatoes, oregano and a splash of water. Season, cover and simmer gently for 30-40 minutes, stirring now and then.
Cook the spaghetti in well-salted boiling water until al dente, then drain, saving a mugful of water.
Toss the pasta through the sauce with a splash of pasta water. Serve with grated Parmesan and a drizzle of oil.

name: Spaghetti Carbonara
blurb: Silky egg and pecorino sauce with crisp guanciale and lots of black pepper.
method: Boil the spaghetti in well-salted water until al dente.
Meanwhile, fry the guanciale in a dry pan over medium heat until the fat renders and it turns crisp and golden.
Beat the eggs and yolk with the pecorino, Parmesan and black pepper in a bowl.
Drain the pasta, reserving a mug of the water. Take the pan of guanciale off the heat and add the pasta, tossing in the fat.
Pour in the egg mixture and toss quickly, adding splashes of pasta water until you have a glossy sauce that coats every strand.
Serve at once with extra pecorino and pepper.

name: Classic Beef Lasagne
blurb: Layers of rich ragu, creamy bechamel and pasta baked until bubbling.
ingredients: 1 onion, 1 carrot, 1 celery stick, all finely chopped
method: Fry the onion, carrot and celery in oil for 10 minutes, add garlic, then brown the mince.
Stir in puree, wine, tomatoes and seasoning. Simmer gently for 45 minutes until thick.
For the bechamel, melt the butter, stir in the flour and cook for 2 minutes, then whisk in the milk a little at a time until smooth and thickened. Add nutmeg and half the Parmesan.
Heat oven to 190C fan. Layer ragu, pasta sheets and bechamel in a dish, repeating and finishing with bechamel.
Scatter over the remaining Parmesan and bake for 35-40 minutes until golden and bubbling.
Rest for 10 minutes before cutting.

name: Cacio e Pepe
blurb: Three ingredients, all technique: pecorino, pepper and starchy pasta water.
method: Toast the crushed pepper in a wide pan for 30 seconds, then add a ladle of water and let it simmer.
Cook the pasta in minimal well-salted water so it becomes very starchy, until just shy of al dente.
Transfer the pasta to the pepper pan with a little of its water and finish cooking, tossing.
Off the heat, add a splash more water and the pecorino in stages, tossing hard to form a creamy sauce.
Loosen with water as needed and serve immediately.

name: Spaghetti al Pomodoro
blurb: The purest tomato pasta: good oil, garlic, basil and a long gentle simmer.
method: Warm the oil with the garlic over low heat until fragrant but not coloured.
Crush in the tomatoes by hand, add a pinch of salt and the sugar, and simmer gently for 20 minutes until jammy.
Tear in most of the basil.
Cook the spaghetti until al dente, then drain and toss through the sauce with a little pasta water.
Finish with the rest of the basil and a good drizzle of oil.

name: Penne all'Arrabbiata
blurb: Angry little tomato sauce with plenty of chilli and garlic.
method: Gently fry the garlic and chilli flakes in the oil until the garlic is pale gold.
Add the tomatoes and a pinch of salt, and simmer for 15 minutes until thickened.
Cook the penne until al dente and drain, keeping some pasta water.
Toss the pasta through the sauce with a splash of water, then stir in the parsley and serve.

name: Trofie with Basil Pesto
blurb: Fresh basil pesto with potato and green beans, the Ligurian way.
method: Blitz the basil, pine nuts, both cheeses, garlic and oil to a coarse pesto. Season.
Boil the pasta, adding the potato at the same time and the beans for the last 4 minutes.
Drain, saving a little water, and toss everything with the pesto, loosening with pasta water.
Serve straight away, without reheating the pesto.

name: Bucatini all'Amatriciana
blurb: Guanciale, tomato and pecorino with a gentle chilli hum.
method: Fry the guanciale gently until crisp, then lift out half and set aside.
Add the chilli and wine to the pan, let it reduce, then add the tomatoes and simmer for 15 minutes.
Cook the bucatini until al dente and drain.
Toss the pasta in the sauce with the pecorino and a little pasta water, then top with the reserved guanciale.

name: Mushroom Risotto
blurb: Creamy slow-stirred rice with mixed mushrooms, thyme and Parmesan.
method: Fry the mushrooms in a little butter over high heat until golden, then set aside.
Soften the onion in the same pan, add garlic and thyme, then stir in the rice for 2 minutes.
Pour in the wine and let it absorb, then add the hot stock a ladle at a time, stirring, until the rice is creamy and al dente (about 18 minutes).
Stir the mushrooms back in with the butter and Parmesan, cover and rest for 2 minutes.
Loosen with a little stock and serve.

name: Risotto alla Milanese
blurb: Golden saffron risotto, rich with butter and Parmesan.
ingredients: 1.2 litres hot chicken or vegetable stock
1 tbsp bone marrow or extra butter (optional)
method: Steep the saffron in a little warm stock.
Soften the onion in half the butter, then toast the rice for 2 minutes.
Add the wine, let it absorb, then add stock a ladle at a time, stirring constantly.
Halfway through, stir in the saffron stock. Continue until the rice is al dente and creamy.
Beat in the rest of the butter and the Parmesan off the heat, rest 2 minutes and serve.

name: Gnocchi alla Sorrentina
blurb: Potato gnocchi baked in tomato sauce with molten mozzarella.
method: Fry the garlic in the oil, add the tomatoes and a pinch of salt, and simmer 15 minutes until thick. Tear in most of the basil.
Boil the gnocchi until they float, then drain.
Fold the gnocchi through the sauce in an ovenproof pan, dot with mozzarella and scatter with Parmesan.
Grill or bake at 220C for 8-10 minutes until bubbling and blistered. Finish with basil.

name: Chicken Parmigiana
blurb: Crumbed chicken breast under tomato sauce and melted mozzarella.
method: Simmer the passata with the garlic and a pinch of salt for 15 minutes.
Coat each chicken piece in flour, then egg, then the breadcrumbs mixed with half the Parmesan.
Shallow fry for 3 minutes each side until golden, then transfer to a baking dish.
Spoon over the tomato sauce, top with mozzarella and the rest of the Parmesan.
Bake at 200C fan for 12-15 minutes until melted and bubbling. Finish with basil.

name: Melanzane alla Parmigiana
blurb: Baked layers of fried aubergine, tomato sauce and Parmesan.
method: Salt the aubergine slices for 20 minutes, then pat dry and fry in oil until golden on both sides. Drain on kitchen paper.
Make a quick sauce: fry the garlic, add tomatoes and basil, simmer 20 minutes and season.
Layer sauce, aubergine, mozzarella and Parmesan in a dish, repeating and finishing with Parmesan.
Bake at 180C fan for 35 minutes until golden. Rest 10 minutes before serving.

name: Spaghetti Puttanesca
blurb: Punchy sauce of olives, capers, anchovy, garlic and chilli.
method: Melt the anchovies with the garlic and chilli in olive oil over low heat.
Add the capers, olives and tomatoes, and simmer for 12-15 minutes.
Cook the spaghetti until al dente and drain.
Toss the pasta through the sauce with parsley and a little pasta water.

name: Osso Buco with Gremolata
blurb: Braised veal shin in white wine and stock, with a bright lemon gremolata.
ingredients: 1 onion, 1 carrot, 1 celery stick, finely diced
For gremolata: zest of 1 lemon, 1 garlic clove, handful parsley, all finely chopped
method: Tie each piece of shin around the middle, dust with flour and brown in oil in a casserole. Set aside.
Soften the vegetables in the same pan for 10 minutes.
Add the wine and reduce by half, then the stock, tomatoes and bay. Return the meat.
Cover and cook at 150C fan for 2 hours until the meat is falling from the bone.
Mix the gremolata ingredients and scatter over just before serving, with the sauce.

name: Minestrone
blurb: Chunky vegetable and bean soup with a handful of small pasta.
ingredients: Handful of kale or cabbage, shredded
method: Soften the onion, carrot and celery in olive oil for 10 minutes, then add the garlic and courgette.
Add the tomatoes, beans and stock, and simmer for 15 minutes.
Stir in the pasta and greens and cook for another 10 minutes until the pasta is tender.
Season well and serve with grated Parmesan or a spoon of pesto.

name: Pork Ragu Bianco with Pappardelle
blurb: A white ragu of slow-cooked pork with wine, milk and sage, no tomato.
ingredients: 800g pork shoulder, cut into large chunks
Few sage leaves and 1 rosemary sprig
method: Brown the pork all over in a casserole, then remove.
Soften the onion and garlic, return the pork, add the wine and reduce by half.
Add the stock and herbs, cover and cook at 150C fan for 2 hours until the pork shreds easily.
Shred the meat in the pan, add the milk and simmer 15 minutes to a creamy sauce.
Toss with cooked pappardelle and plenty of Parmesan.

name: Tomato & Mozzarella Orzo
blurb: One-pan orzo cooked risotto-style with roasted tomatoes and torn mozzarella.
method: Fry the cherry tomatoes in the oil over high heat until blistered and starting to collapse.
Add the garlic and puree for 1 minute, then stir in the orzo.
Add the stock a third at a time, stirring, until the orzo is creamy and tender, about 12 minutes.
Off the heat, fold through the mozzarella and basil and serve.

name: Veal Saltimbocca
blurb: Thin veal escalopes with prosciutto and sage in a quick wine and butter sauce.
method: Lay a slice of prosciutto and 2 sage leaves on each escalope and press or secure with a cocktail stick.
Dust the meat side lightly with flour.
Fry prosciutto-side up in butter for 2 minutes, flip and cook 1 minute more. Remove.
Add the wine to the pan, scrape up the bits, bubble to a light sauce and finish with lemon and a knob of butter.
Spoon over the veal and serve straight away.

name: Tuna, Lemon & Chilli Spaghetti
blurb: Storecupboard hero: good tinned tuna, lemon, garlic and chilli.
method: Cook the spaghetti until al dente.
Gently warm the oil, garlic and chilli in a pan, then add the tuna with its oil, breaking it up.
Add the lemon zest and a splash of pasta water.
Toss the drained pasta through with the lemon juice and parsley, then serve.

name: Sausage & Fennel Rigatoni
blurb: Italian sausage meat, fennel seeds and a splash of cream on rigatoni.
method: Fry the sausage meat hard, breaking it into craggy pieces until deeply browned.
Add the fennel seeds, chilli and garlic for 1 minute, then the wine and reduce by half.
Stir in the cream and a splash of pasta water to make a sauce.
Toss with the cooked rigatoni and Parmesan, loosening with pasta water as needed.

name: Panzanella with Burrata
blurb: Torn sourdough soaked in tomato juices with basil, capers and creamy burrata.
method: Toss the tomatoes with a good pinch of salt and leave for 10 minutes to release their juices.
Soak the onion in the vinegar for 10 minutes.
Toast or griddle the bread until lightly charred, then toss with the tomatoes, onion, capers and oil.
Leave for 10 minutes so the bread softens, tear through the basil, then serve with burrata torn over.
